text:
Recommended protocol: freeze splits, item mappings, dataset routing, preprocessing seed=0, training/evaluation seeds=42, and the exact 200 validation users plus 99 unique negatives per user in each category. Record code, environment, hardware and effective configuration, including SASREC_EPOCHS=200. Predeclare validation frequency, patience, checkpoint eligibility and deterministic tie-breaking; select by the pinned four-category macro HR@10. Save weights, architecture/configuration, optimizer, scheduler and RNG states for resumption. Cap aggregate search at 43,200 GPU-seconds across concurrent slots, charging diagnostics and failures and reserving time for export checks.

Retain per-user hit indicators. For comparisons, bootstrap paired user differences within each category, then average the four category differences equally; use a fixed bootstrap seed. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates, excluding training-seed variation and selection bias ([paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). Log every validation query and candidate: repeated validation reuse can overfit selection, so selected validation scores remain exploratory ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings; retain the pinned metric and limit claims accordingly ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Bound diagnostics using fixed users, batches, catalog chunks and runtime caps, with separate RNG streams; retain required full-catalog recommendations for twenty training users. Report diagnostic definitions separately, using only observed histories and metadata. Reload the selected artifact through exported inference and compare scores within declared tolerances, top-10 rankings and HR@10 against the trained model in evaluation mode. Check padding, truncation, masking, item IDs and category routing. Record precision/backend settings: mathematically equivalent computations need not be bitwise identical ([PyTorch numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)).
